source_name: Zaštitnik ljudskih prava i sloboda Crne Gore (Ombudsman) — recommendations and news
why_relevant: Publishes individual recommendations (preporuke) and annual reports; complaints about non-enforcement of court decisions, prolonged proceedings and discrimination frequently involve banks, debtors and enforcement agents. Not a financial ombudsman, so banking coverage is partial but occasionally very specific.

source_name: CEZAP — Centar za zaštitu potrošača Crne Gore (Montenegrin consumer protection centre)
why_relevant: The main consumer NGO (since 1999) runs an advice line and a complaints database covering financial services and insurance, classifies complaints by resolution route, and escalates to inspections. Its news/analysis output names banks and practices that regulators have not yet acted on — early-warning signal.

source_name: Upravni sud Crne Gore — Odluke (Administrative Court decisions)
why_relevant: Judicial review venue for AZZK and CBCG administrative acts. Judgments restate the agency's factual findings (market shares, fee structures) and reveal which enforcement decisions were annulled — essential for judging whether an agency decision actually stood.

source_name: Privredni sud Crne Gore (Commercial Court), Podgorica — decisions and notices
why_relevant: Commercial disputes involving banks, payment institutions, bankruptcy/liquidation and enforcement over collateral; court notices identify distressed counterparties and disputes over fees and contract terms.

source_name: sudovi.me — central portal of Montenegrin courts (Sudovi Crne Gore)
why_relevant: Umbrella portal listing every court and its decisions section (Vrhovni, Apelacioni, Upravni, Privredni, Viši and Osnovni sudovi) — the entry point for systematically snowballing all judicial sources bearing on banks and payment firms.

source_name: PROPISINET.ME — Sudska praksa sudova Crne Gore and consolidated legislation
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator that indexes Montenegrin case law against the statutes it applies (including Zakon o zaštiti konkurencije and Zakon o zaštiti potrošača — korisnika finansijskih usluga), making it far faster to find bank/fee-related rulings than the raw court sites.

source_name: Uprava za inspekcijske poslove — Odsjek za tržišnu inspekciju (Market Inspection), annual work reports
why_relevant: Market inspection acts on consumer complaints about economic interests, including services; its annual reports quantify complaints received, inspections and sanctions, and describe recurring unfair-practice patterns. Complements CBCG where the conduct is commercial rather than prudential.

source_name: wapi.gov.me document endpoint — Montenegrin government document store
why_relevant: All gov.me ministry and inspectorate PDFs (inspection reports, consumer-policy programmes, Chapter 8/28 negotiation documents) are served from this UUID-keyed endpoint; recognising the pattern is what makes automated harvesting of government enforcement documents feasible.

source_name: Akcioni plan za ispunjenje završnih mjerila u poglavlju 8 – Konkurencija (EU accession Chapter 8 action plan)
why_relevant: EU accession benchmarking documents candidly assess AZZK's enforcement capacity, case throughput and known weaknesses — the calibration needed to know how much absence of decisions means absence of problems versus absence of capacity.

source_name: Skupština Crne Gore — zakoni.skupstina.me legislative document repository
why_relevant: Draft laws and their explanatory memoranda (obrazloženje) for competition, consumer-protection of financial-services users, and interbank-fee legislation contain impact assessments and market data used to justify intervention — plus AZZK opinions submitted to parliament.

source_name: Zakon o međubankarskim naknadama i posebnim pravilima za poslovanje sa platnim karticama (Sl. list CG 145/21) — interchange regulation, via Službeni list / CBCG legislation page
why_relevant: Montenegro's IFR-equivalent capping interchange and setting card-scheme business rules; the legal hook for any interchange dispute, and the reference point for supervisory or competition action on card fees. Reported as published in Official Gazette of Montenegro no. 145/21 (verify text at source).

source_name: CBCG — Prinudna naplata: podaci i pretraga blokiranih pravnih lica i preduzetnika (register of blocked accounts)
why_relevant: Searchable register of legal entities with blocked accounts under forced collection (prinudna naplata) — a direct enforcement-side dataset showing distress and the volume/duration of account blockades running through the payment system.

source_name: BDK Advokati — Montenegro competition-law commentary (sr/en)
why_relevant: Regional law firm that publishes prompt, substantive notes on AZZK decisions (e.g. the first conditional clearance, Telemach/M-Kabl 2015) in Serbian and English — a practical early alert layer and interpretation aid for decisions published only as scanned PDFs.

source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine — Montenegrin bank & regulator domains
why_relevant: Montenegrin bank and regulator sites rotate/delete PDFs; Wayback is the only route to historic IR pages, annual report PDFs and press releases that were removed from cbcg.me, ckb.me, nlb.me, erstebank.me, hipotekarnabanka.com.

source_name: Archive.today (archive.ph) — snapshots of ME bank/press pages
why_relevant: Complements Wayback for JS-heavy or robots-excluded Montenegrin bank pages and news items; often holds captures Wayback lacks.

source_name: CBCG — Publikacije / Arhiva (publication archive)
why_relevant: Time-series of Financial Stability Reports, macro bulletins and annual reports back to ~2006; the normalising source for sector aggregates against which individual bank disclosures can be verified.

source_name: Portal otvorenih podataka Crne Gore (Montenegro Open Data Portal)
why_relevant: Government open-data portal with a 'Finansije' category; machine-readable datasets from ministries and agencies, an alternative durable channel when institutional HTML pages rotate.

source_name: eUprava Crne Gore (e-government service portal)
why_relevant: Directory of official electronic services incl. CRPS registry and financial-statement filing/access services; pointer to where structured company data actually lives.

source_name: Montenegroberza (Montenegro Stock Exchange) — issuer disclosures
why_relevant: Listed ME banks (e.g. Hipotekarna banka) file annual/semi-annual/quarterly reports and material-event notices with the exchange; an independent archive of the same filings banks post on IR pages.

source_name: SeeCapitalMarkets — Montenegro Berza data aggregator
why_relevant: Third-party normaliser of Montenegroberza listings and historical instrument prices; useful cross-check and continuity when the exchange's own archive is reorganised.

source_name: Moody's Ratings — Montenegro sovereign and EU release calendar
why_relevant: Sovereign rating actions and credit opinions on Montenegro; the EU sovereign release calendar (CRA Reg. 462/2013) gives pre-announced dates, letting collection be scheduled rather than polled.

source_name: S&P Global Ratings — Montenegro sovereign / bank ratings
why_relevant: Second independent rating opinion on the ME sovereign and on regionally-owned banks operating in ME; rating rationales summarise bank financials and often cite figures not otherwise republished.

source_name: Fitch Ratings / Scope Ratings — Montenegro sovereign coverage
why_relevant: Fitch and Scope both maintain ME sovereign coverage with scheduled review dates; rating commentary is a compact, dated, independent read on banking-sector and fiscal conditions.

source_name: countryeconomy.com — Montenegro credit rating history
why_relevant: Free, dated time series of every S&P/Moody's/Fitch/DBRS action on Montenegro — a usable substitute for the paywalled agency archives when building a rating-history series.

source_name: TheGlobalEconomy.com — Montenegro sovereign credit rating series
why_relevant: Numeric-scaled rating time series for ME, convenient for charting and for detecting the date of any change without agency access.

source_name: FXEmpire — Montenegro credit ratings & outlooks
why_relevant: Aggregates S&P/Moody's/Fitch/DBRS/Scope actions on ME with outlooks and dates; a third redundancy layer for rating-event detection.

source_name: Cbonds — rating actions and bond data feed (SEE/Montenegro)
why_relevant: Financial data vendor that republishes rating-action news for regional banks and sovereigns and carries ME eurobond data; useful pointer feed for events behind agency paywalls.

source_name: EMIS (ISI Emerging Markets) — Montenegro company profiles & financials
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator that normalises ME bank financial statements into comparable multi-year series and retains data after the original filings disappear from bank sites.
